section_summary: This section documents complaints about Japanese use of American trade marks, product designs, national symbols, and misleading statements of origin. It includes correspondence about Edison lamps, needle packages, and a disputed cosmetics mark; inquiries about whether “Made in USA” could refer to the Japanese place name Usa; and translations of Japanese trade mark and unfair competition laws.

subfiles.title: File note on Edison-stamped Japanese bulbs
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch about Japanese bulbs marked “Edison”.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references the Alexandria despatch to the Edison file.

subfiles.title: Reported fraudulent marking of Edison lamps
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese automobile bulbs sold in Alexandria under the “Edison” name.
subfiles.summary: Russell describes an Alexandria importer’s sale of Japanese bulbs marked “Edison” and forwards correspondence indicating that the Japanese manufacturer lacked rights to that mark.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to Kobe about Stanley Edison lamps
subfiles.about: Requests investigation of Stanley Auto Lamps Company’s authority to use “Edison”.
subfiles.summary: Blackard compares Stanley bulbs with genuine Mazda Edison bulbs, notes missing origin markings, and asks the Kobe consul to investigate the maker and its rights.

subfiles.title: Tokyo investigation of Edison bulb mark
subfiles.about: Identifies the Tokyo bulb manufacturer and the Japanese registrant of “Edison”.
subfiles.summary: Garrels reports that Tokyo Kitano Shoten made the bulbs, while International General Electric held Japan’s Edison registration.

subfiles.title: File note on General Electric patent protest
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch enclosing an anti-General Electric leaflet.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Grew’s despatch to the General Electric file.

subfiles.title: Leaflet issued by Society Opposing the General Electric Patents
subfiles.about: Transmits a leaflet distributed at a Tokyo meeting against General Electric bulb patents.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that about 2,000 attended the protest. He observes that speakers spent little time on the patent applications and instead made antisemitic attacks, possibly reflecting broader political influences.

subfiles.title: Statement and song opposing General Electric patents
subfiles.from: Society Opposing the General Electric Patents
subfiles.about: Calls for opposition to General Electric’s bulb patents and litigation.
subfiles.summary: The society argues that General Electric’s patents and lawsuits threaten Japan’s bulb industry, asks for public support, and advances antisemitic conspiracy claims. Its closing song attacks General Electric and Mazda.

subfiles.title: Japanese metal polish bearing American imagery
subfiles.about: Flags a Japanese metal-polish container depicting Washington and United States symbols.
subfiles.summary: Grab asks State to consider whether the container misleads buyers about its origin.

subfiles.title: State Department routing notation
subfiles.about: Records internal handling of the preceding correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Mostly illegible State Department communications and records notation.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about assigning Japanese trade marks to a Uruguayan affiliate
subfiles.about: Requests information on a purported Uruguay–Japan treaty affecting trade mark ownership.
subfiles.summary: Grab forwards patent agents’ inquiry about assigning Japanese registrations to a Uruguayan affiliate.

subfiles.title: Trade mark assignment inquiry
subfiles.to: Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
subfiles.about: Asks whether a Montevideo affiliate can acquire Japanese meat-product trade mark registrations.
subfiles.summary: The firm describes registrations held by a Japanese dealer and requests the purported Uruguay–Japan treaty and guidance.

subfiles.title: Reply on purported Uruguay–Japan commercial treaty
subfiles.about: Responds to the trade mark assignment inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Welles says State has received no report that Uruguay and Japan concluded the alleged treaty.

subfiles.title: Japanese needle folder with American symbols
subfiles.about: Complains that Japanese needle packaging suggests American manufacture.
subfiles.summary: Grab describes a folder showing American national imagery and the warship “Iowa,” despite “Made in Japan” markings. He cites Japanese trade mark and unfair competition provisions and sends the packaging to State.

subfiles.title: Consumer complaint about Japanese needle book
subfiles.about: Reports that a Japanese needle book appeared American or British.
subfiles.summary: Learmonth describes an eagle, the warship “Iowa,” and a crown mark on the packaging.

subfiles.title: State reply concerning Japanese needle packaging
subfiles.about: Reports that the American embassy will seek action against the misleading needle folder.
subfiles.summary: Moore says State is sending the complaint and package to Tokyo for presentation under Japanese unfair competition law and the industrial property convention.

subfiles.title: Instruction to protest needle-folder design
subfiles.about: Directs the embassy to seek an end to manufacture and sale of the needle folder.
subfiles.summary: Moore describes the American flag, shield, and warship imagery as a misleading suggestion of American origin and instructs Grew to raise the matter with Japanese authorities.

subfiles.title: Analysis of Japanese unfair competition law
subfiles.about: Reviews a new Japanese law addressing imitation marks and false origin claims.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum notes possible remedies for copied trade marks and misleading origin statements, but questions access for foreign owners without a Japanese residence or office. It proposes asking the Tokyo embassy how the law will operate.

subfiles.title: Resolution of needle-wrapper complaint
subfiles.about: Reports the Japanese manufacturer’s promise to remove American symbols from a needle folder.
subfiles.summary: Grew encloses the embassy’s protest, Japan’s reply, and a corrected wrapper.

subfiles.title: Embassy note protesting needle wrapper
subfiles.about: Requests Japanese action against needle packaging that suggests United States origin.
subfiles.summary: Grew objects to the warship, flag, and shield imagery and asks Hirota to prevent manufacture and sale of the folder.

subfiles.title: Japanese Foreign Office reply on needle wrapper
subfiles.about: Reports a voluntary change to the complained-of needle packaging.
subfiles.summary: Hirota says the maker promised to remove the warship name, flag, stars, and shield. The legal question under the convention and Japanese law was deferred.

subfiles.title: State update to Commerce on needle packaging
subfiles.about: Reports the Japanese manufacturer’s promise to discontinue the objectionable needle folder.
subfiles.summary: Sayre forwards the embassy despatch and Japanese reply documenting the changed folder.

subfiles.title: Enclosure charge slip
subfiles.about: Tracks an enclosure’s internal circulation.
subfiles.summary: Records file charges and clerk entries for an enclosure.

subfiles.title: Commerce forwarding letter on trade mark infringements
subfiles.from: Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
subfiles.about: Forwards an internal memorandum about Japanese trade mark and label infringements.
subfiles.summary: The liaison officer sends Murphy the Commercial Laws Division memorandum.

subfiles.title: Unfair trade practices in Japan
subfiles.to: Director, Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
subfiles.about: Surveys complaints and attempted remedies concerning Japanese imitations of foreign products.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum describes copied marks, packaging, and origin labels in Japanese exports, with examples involving pens, milk, tools, toothbrushes, belting, and publications. It recounts discussions with State and Japanese officials, including inspection and investigation measures. Identifying particular manufacturers remained a major obstacle.

subfiles.title: File note on CELLULOID mark
subfiles.about: Points to correspondence about Japanese infringement of the CELLULOID mark.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references the Celluloid Corporation complaint to its separate file.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese patent and trade mark laws
subfiles.about: Points to a request for a copy of Japanese patent and trade mark laws.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references McCauley’s request to another file.

subfiles.title: File note on PARAFLOW design
subfiles.about: Points to a request to investigate Japanese treatment of the PARAFLOW design.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Standard Oil Development Company’s registration concern.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about a Japanese town named Usa
subfiles.from: Edward A. Rossit; United States Information Service
subfiles.to: United States Information Service; Department of State
subfiles.about: Asks whether Japanese goods can be marked “USA” because of a town named Usa.
subfiles.summary: Rossit’s question is forwarded to State for an answer.

subfiles.title: Reply to Rossit on Usa
subfiles.about: Confirms a Japanese place called Usa and refers customs-marking rules to Customs.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton locates Usa on Kyushu and directs Rossit to the New York Customs House for import-marking requirements.

subfiles.title: Complaint about toilet tissue marked from Usa
subfiles.about: Complains that Japanese toilet tissue and an eagle mark appeared American.
subfiles.summary: Cosentino says he had believed the tissue was made in the United States.

subfiles.title: Reply to Cosentino
subfiles.about: Refers the toilet-tissue marking complaint to Treasury.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton explains that Treasury administers American import-marking law.

subfiles.title: Referral of Cosentino complaint to Treasury
subfiles.about: Sends Treasury Cosentino’s complaint for consideration and reply.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the letter about Japanese toilet tissue with an apparently American mark.

subfiles.title: File note on matches marked Made in Sweden
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum about a purported Japanese town named Sweden.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references a discussion with F. A. Eble about match-box origin claims.

subfiles.title: Customs inquiry about Usa
subfiles.about: Requests authoritative information on the Japanese name Usa for import-marking enforcement.
subfiles.summary: Customs seeks confirmation and spelling of Usa after a complaint about merchandise marked “Made in USA.”

subfiles.title: State geographic reply about Usa
subfiles.about: Explains the historical Japanese place name Usa.
subfiles.summary: State identifies Usa county, Minami Usa, and another Usa on Shikoku, citing an 1889 place-name dictionary.

subfiles.title: Customs acknowledgment of Usa information
subfiles.about: Acknowledges State’s geographic information for a “Made in USA” case.
subfiles.summary: Customs says the information will help dispose of the marking complaint.

subfiles.title: File note on WASHINGTON canvas-shoe mark
subfiles.about: Points to a clipping asserting Japanese ownership of the WASHINGTON shoe mark.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references a Straits Times notice about Nippon Rubber Company’s mark.

subfiles.title: Translation of revised Japanese trade mark law
subfiles.about: Transmits a translation of Japan’s 1938 trade mark law revision.
subfiles.summary: Grew forwards the embassy’s translation of Law No. 4.

subfiles.title: Japanese Law No. 4 revising trade mark law
subfiles.about: Deletes second paragraphs of Articles 13 and 14 of the trade mark law.
subfiles.summary: The law leaves its enforcement date to an imperial ordinance.

subfiles.title: Translation of revised unfair competition law
subfiles.about: Transmits translations of Japan’s 1938 unfair competition revision and consolidated law.
subfiles.summary: Grew forwards both the amendment and a revised translation of the full law.

subfiles.title: Japanese Law No. 2 revising unfair competition law
subfiles.about: Extends unfair competition rules to confusing use of another business’s name or symbols.
subfiles.summary: The amendment adds protection for business identity and adjusts related exceptions and references. Enforcement is left to an imperial ordinance.

subfiles.title: Consolidated Japanese Unfair Competition Law
subfiles.about: Sets remedies and restrictions for confusing marks, false origins, disparagement, and foreign emblems.
subfiles.summary: The translated law permits damages or cessation for specified unfair acts and addresses false origin statements and use of foreign national symbols. It states exceptions for generic names and some patent or trade mark rights, and limits claims by foreigners without a local domicile or business unless a treaty provides otherwise.

subfiles.title: Christmas cards believed manufactured in Japan
subfiles.about: Reports suspicion that cards marked “Made in U S A” originated in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Byington forwards a card after the Montreal Daily Herald editor raised the Usa-name concern.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing clipping on Japanese place-name claims
subfiles.about: Forwards a clipping alleging deceptive Japanese place names and asks about federal departments.
subfiles.summary: The correspondent cites claims about Usa, Sweden, and Macclesfield and requests a guide to government departments.

subfiles.title: Reply to Garneey
subfiles.about: Responds to a request for publications explaining federal departments.
subfiles.summary: Spaulding encloses State Department publications and points to the Congressional Directory for descriptions of federal agencies.

subfiles.title: Federal Trade Commission inquiry on Usa
subfiles.about: Asks whether Usa exists in Japan and whether its name was recently changed.
subfiles.summary: Kielland seeks the place-name history for a merchandise-origin investigation.

subfiles.title: State reply to Federal Trade Commission on Usa
subfiles.about: Explains that Usa is a historical Japanese place name.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton identifies Usa county, Minami Usa, and the Shikoku namesake, and says the places are not known as industrial centers.

subfiles.title: Holyoke postmaster inquiry about “Printed in U.S.A.”
subfiles.about: Seeks guidance for American Tissue Mills on abbreviating United States in its printed mark.
subfiles.summary: Dowd asks whether the firm should change its inscription because of a reported Japanese town named U.S.A.

subfiles.title: Post Office Solicitor’s letter on Usa rumor
subfiles.about: Says the Post Office lacks authoritative information about a Japanese place called U.S.A.
subfiles.summary: The solicitor recounts press claims and suggests seeking information from State.

subfiles.title: State reply to Holyoke postmaster
subfiles.about: Provides the known geography of Usa but leaves American Tissue Mills’ wording to the company.
subfiles.summary: Baker quotes earlier State replies identifying historical Usa and Minami Usa. He says State cannot decide the firm’s printing policy.

subfiles.title: M. Stein trade mark complaint
subfiles.about: Seeks help opposing a former Japanese customer’s application for the “M. Stein” mark.
subfiles.summary: The company says Ota Eijiro Shoten applied to register its mark for soaps and asks State to intervene before the opposition deadline.

subfiles.title: State reply to M. Stein Cosmetic Co.
subfiles.about: Advises formal Japanese opposition proceedings against the disputed trade mark application.
subfiles.summary: Hackworth says the company should use Japanese legal procedures before the deadline; diplomatic intervention is inappropriate without them. He sends the case to the consul general for proper assistance.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Tokyo consul on M. Stein mark
subfiles.about: Forwards the M. Stein complaint and State’s reply for consular guidance.
subfiles.summary: Moore sends Cameron copies concerning the presumed Japanese registration application.

subfiles.title: File note on imitated American pencils
subfiles.about: Points to an allegation that Japanese pencils exported to China imitated an American mark.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references the pencil complaint to another file.

subfiles.title: CELLULOID trade mark case jacket
subfiles.about: Labels a case on Japanese dealers’ alleged infringement of the CELLULOID mark.
subfiles.summary: The jacket carries the case title and handling instructions.
